title: Heavier in a Lift? N = m(g+a) Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A swing drops and your stomach floats, a diver feels weightless in the air, astronauts float in their station. Did their weight really change? Diya takes the hospital lift up: as it starts she feels heavier, as it stops at the top floor she feels lighter. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn apparent weight and weightlessness, the last lesson of the chapter.

Diya, 50 kg, stands on a scale in a live lift. As it speeds up going up at 1 m/s², the scale jumps from 50.0 to 55.1 kg; at a steady 2 m/s it is back to 50; as it slows near the top it drops to 44.9 kg, while a graph of the reading against time steps up, flat and down. A slow-mo replay of the stop shows the velocity pointing up while the acceleration points down. We derive N = m(g + a) from Newton's second law step by step, compare going up and slowing with going down and speeding up, follow a falling box with a scale and an apple to weightlessness, and see why astronauts in orbit float even though gravity still pulls on them. Then a worked example, the exam trap about velocity, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
